items.title: European CLO issuance through September 2026 — volume and AAA clearing spreads
items.query: European CLO US CLO issuance AAA BB spread October 2026 Creditflux Trepp PitchBook LCD
items.excerpt: European CLO issuance reached €94.9bn across 229 deals year-to-date through September 2026. September 2026 printed €10.7bn across 24 deals: €7.6bn of new issue across 17 deals and €3.1bn of refinancings and resets across 7 deals. September AAA clearing spreads averaged 124 bps on European new issue and 120 bps on refi/reset paper (a 4 bps refi/reset discount).

items.excerpt: Over 100 European CLO warehouses remained open entering Q4 2026, with Bank of America forecasting roughly €60bn of full-year 2026 European CLO refi and reset volume. European leveraged loan spreads compressed from ~355 bps toward ~350 bps, squeezing equity arbitrage against tight AAA liabilities while CLO equity cash-on-cash distributions averaged 12-16% annualised against depressed equity NAV marks.

items.title: Altice International capital structure, 2027 maturity wall, and €750m unrestricted drop-down
items.query: Altice International Virgin Media O2 VodafoneZiggo leveraged loan bond restructuring October 2026 9fin Octus Debtwire
items.excerpt: Altice International carries roughly $9.0bn (approx. €8.0bn) of total debt, with roughly €3.1bn maturing in 2027, facing tight creditor NDA expiration deadlines in late October 2026. In November 2025, Altice International designated Altice Portugal and Altice Caribbean as unrestricted subsidiaries and raised €750m of 12% financing against them. Cash and undrawn revolving credit stood near €528m against roughly €346m of trailing 12-month negative free cash flow.

items.title: Altice International creditor cooperation agreement renewal and secondary bond marks

items.excerpt: Holders representing roughly 90% of Altice International's debt (including Arini, Elliott, Sona, Diameter, Invesco, BlackRock, and Ares, advised by Houlihan Lokey and Milbank) renewed their cooperation agreement for 18 months through March 2027. Altice International senior secured bonds traded in the mid-to-low 60s (approx. 63 pts) amid disputes over sponsor compensation and holdco bridge treatment.

items.title: Thames Water 16 Oct 2026 binding Class B TSA, £5.4bn upsized super-senior ask, and L&VW RP2 plan
items.query: Thames Water restructuring Class A Class B bondholders Ofwat October 2026 9fin Octus London Valley Water consortium
items.excerpt: On 16 October 2026, Thames Water entered a legally binding Class B Transaction Support Agreement (TSA) across its ~£16.0bn Whole Business Securitisation (WBS) stack (~£20.0bn total group debt): holders of over 60% of ~£1.0bn Class B junior debt agreed to a full principal write-off in exchange for ~5.9% post-restructured equity plus rights in a £150m new equity raise. Thames Water has drawn £2.65bn of its £3.0bn super-senior facility and seeks a £2.4bn upsize to £5.4bn to bridge operations to autumn 2027 past the March 2027 Stable Platform expiry, while the senior Class A London & Valley Water (L&VW) consortium (including Elliott and Silver Point, advised by Akin Gump and Jefferies) pursues a ~£10.0bn Restructuring Plan 2 (RP2) recapitalisation still awaiting formal Ofwat acceptance.

items.title: Fitch US & European leveraged loan default rate, Top Market Concern list, and LME repeat-default rate
items.query: Fitch Leveraged Loan Default Report October 2026 Top Market Concern 3.6% LME repeat default
items.excerpt: Fitch's trailing 12-month US institutional leveraged loan default rate stood at 3.6% entering Q4 2026, while the combined Top Market Concern and Tier 2 watch list represented 10.3% to 10.6% of the index. Distressed debt exchanges (LMEs) accounted for over 55% of default events, and roughly 55% of issuers completing an out-of-court LME re-defaulted or required a second restructuring within 18 to 24 months. European leveraged loan default forecasts sit at 3.8% to 4.8%.

items.excerpt: Fitch Ratings and PitchBook LCD data show aggregate BDC Payment-in-Kind (PIK) income reached roughly 8.0% of total BDC interest and dividend income in 2026, flattering headline net investment income and dividend coverage. While median headline BDC non-accruals at cost remained at 3.0-4.0%, PitchBook LCD reported over 10.0% of BDC portfolio companies exhibiting broader credit-pressure warning signs. Software and SaaS borrowers represent over 20.0% of direct lending portfolios, ~26.0% of BDC distressed fair-value marks, and over 33.0% (over one-third) of all BDC-held investments showing credit pressure amid AI business-model disruption fears, driving 15-20% public BDC equity discounts to NAV.

Tier-1 US BSL AAA spreads held tight near 118-119 bps over SOFR, while tier-1 US BSL BB spreads widened by roughly 60 bps to ~500 bps over SOFR, stretching the US AAA-to-BB spread differential to ~381.5 bps (up from ~322 bps).

items.title: Fitch US BSL CLO OC cushion split — reinvesting (9.3% Sr / 4.5% Jr) vs post-reinvestment (68.0% Sr / 2.1% Jr)
items.query: Fitch US BSL CLO OC cushion reinvesting 9.3% 4.5% post-reinvestment 68% 2.1% WARF 2026
items.excerpt: Fitch US BSL CLO surveillance data shows reinvesting US BSL CLOs maintain an average Senior OC cushion of 9.3% (930 bps) and an average Junior OC cushion of 4.5% (450 bps), with portfolio WARF stable in the B+/B range near 2750. By contrast, post-reinvestment US BSL CLOs exhibit an average Senior OC cushion above 68.0% (6800 bps) from sequential AAA amortisation ('deleveraging windfall'), while their average Junior OC cushion compresses to 2.1% (210 bps) as residual CCC and defaulted loans concentrate against the unamortised BB/B stack.

items.title: Fitch European CLO collateral quality 'triple squeeze' (WAS 350 bps / 10 bps cushion) and late-October EUR AAA prints (126–129 bps)
items.query: European CLO Junior OC cushion CCC bucket WARF October 2026 Fitch Moody's S&P Creditflux
items.excerpt: Fitch European CLO surveillance entering late October 2026 shows average portfolio Weighted Average Spread (WAS) compressed to ~350 bps (~40 bps below the 10-year average), leaving the average European WAS cushion thin at ~10 bps. Average European WARF cushion stands at ~0.9 points and WARR cushion at ~3.9%, but roughly 10% of sub-10 bp WAS deals face a 'triple squeeze' (WAS cushion <10 bps, WARF cushion <1.0 point, WARR cushion <1.0%), concentrated in late-reinvestment or post-RP vintages where Fitch downgrades target junior 'F' tranches. Meanwhile, late-October European new-issue AAA prints drifted to 126-129 bps on heavy Q4 supply.

items.title: AI data-centre ABS/CMBS boom ($30–40bn/yr) vs Moody's warning on 'circular financing' and 2027–2029 neocloud refinancing cliff
items.query: AI data center debt financing private credit ABS securitization October 2026 Fitch Moody's Bank of England
items.excerpt: Across the projected $2.9tn global data-centre CapEx buildout through 2028 ($1.5tn external debt gap), annual data-centre ABS and CMBS issuance is projected at $30bn-$40bn/yr after data-centre ABS doubled over two years and CMBS tripled. However, Moody's Ratings warned in late 2026 of 'circular financing' correlations (tech giants, chipmakers, and AI developers investing in, lending to, and buying from one another via off-balance-sheet SPVs) and a 2027-2029 loan refinancing cliff for weaker AI and neocloud borrowers carrying floating-rate private credit and PIK-toggle debt if GPU depreciation outpaces debt amortisation.
